# 5. Interaction Flow The management of transport network faults involves an end-to-end process that includes the perception, diagnosis, repair, and verification testing of anomalies (including faults and risks) in the transport network. Depending on the response mode and execution method, it can be divided into reactive fault diagnosis processes and proactive fault handling processes. The former responds to external requests for root cause diagnosis of faults, providing fault repair solutions to assist on-site fault handling, while the latter aims to ensure the normal operation of the transport network based on network operation and maintenance objectives, addressing anomalies that may cause a gap between the real-time network state and the network operation and maintenance objectives, generating solutions and proactively executing them. ## 5.1. Proactive AN L4 Transport Network Fault Management flow Proactive transport network management aims to ensure the normal operation of the transport network in accordance with network operation and maintenance objectives. It addresses anomalies(including faults and risks) and threats—referred to as "potential anomaly" - that may cause deviations between the real-time network state and operational goals, generates solutions, and actively executes them. In the proactive potential hazard management process, the Fault Agent in the network operations layer automatically completes closed-loop handling of potential hazards based on the anomaly management workflow. This includes anomaly detection, analysis, decision-making, and execution of repair measures, achieving self-healing of potential hazards to ensure uninterrupted network operation. [Figure: Fig.3 AN L4 Proactive Fault Management Closed-loop Workflow] The detailed workflow is as: 1. Step 1: The Single-domain Fault Agent continuously monitors network performance metrics and alarm information in real-time. 2. Step 2: Based on the collected data, the Single-domain Fault Agent automatically identifies faults and potential network anomalies, diagnoses root causes and locations, and generates corresponding repair solutions, automatically executes and verifies the result. 3. Step 3: The Single-domain Fault Agent reports the identified anomaly details (including root causes and locations) to the cross-domain OSS system's Fault Agent for oversight. 4. Step 4: The Single-domain Fault Agent submits the completed anomaly resolution case to the OSS system's Fault Agent for archiving and future reference. 5. Step 5: The cross-domain fault agent receives both of resolved and unresolved anomaly records, then dispatches field technicians to verify the identified anomaly on-site, implement the prescribed repair measures. 6. Step6 and Step7:During the on-site handling process, the FME interacts with the service operations layer Copilot and network operations layer Copilot via an app to obtain natural language-based repair guidance. ## 5.2. Reactive AN L4 Transport Network Fault Management flow In the reactive fault diagnosis process, the Fault Agent at the network operations layer performs fault diagnosis and provides repair suggestions by responding in real time to fault analysis requests from the cross-domain management layer. [Figure: Fig.4 AN L4 Reactive Fault Management Closed-loop Workflow] For the reactive fault diagnosis workflow, the Fault Agent in the OSS system of the service operations layer receives complaint/trouble shooting tickets, and awares of the anomalies(including faults and risks) reported by the single-domain fault agent. It then makes decisions and executes the fault repair solution based on the performance data, alarm information, root cause analysis, and repair suggestions provided. The detailed workflow is as: 1. Step 1: The Cross-domain Fault Agent in the OSS system receives a complaint or troubleshooting ticket (Step1). 2. Step 2: The Cross-domain Fault Agent in the OSS system receives performance data, alarm information, anomaly report (e.g., root cause, recover result, repair recommendation, etc.) from the single-domain fault agent (Step2). The Cross-domain Fault Agent automatically correlates tickets and anomaly report. If anomaly is recovered, trigger to close the ticket. 3. Step 3: If the cross-domain agent determines that the repair solution provided by the single-domain agent requires optimization, or if the fault persists after the solution is executed, it will instruct the single-domain agent to initiate a new round of in-depth fault diagnosis. Simultaneously, the cross-domain agent will share relevant contextual information, such as the original work order, diagnostic results from other domains, and historical repair feedback, to assist in the diagnosis. 4. Step 4: Based on the fault repair solution from the Single-domain Fault Agent, the Cross-domain Fault Agent makes a decision and chooses an optimal fault repair solution. 5. Step 5: The Fault Agent in the OSS system assigns the repair task to execute. For faults that cannot be remotely repaired such as hardware faults, fiber interruptions, etc., the cross-domain agent dispatches front-line personnel via a work order system to execute the on-site fault resolution (Step 5.2). Otherwise, it assigns repair operation to the single-domain agent (Step 5.1). 6. Step 6: The single-domain agent automatically executes the corresponding network operations according to the fault repair solution and verifies the results, then reports to the cross-domain agent. 7. Step7 and Step8:During the on-site handling process, the FME interacts with the service operations layer Copilot and network operations layer Copilot via an app to obtain natural language-based repair guidance. It should be noted that repair operation is best assigned or approved by the cross-domain fault agent while network operation may create significant risk, rather than being automatically triggered by the single-domain agent. ## 5.3. 1.1 Fault Management Interface In the Transport Network fault management scenario, the following interface list is involved: | Interface No. | Interface name | Interface provider | Interface user | Function Description of Interface Openness on the Network Side | Reference interface standard document | Related step no.
